My guests today are Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital,
and Geoffrey Canada, founder of Harlem Children's Zone. Geoffrey spent decades helping disadvantaged kids get a great education, but it takes more than that to achieve the American dream. Without savings, you’re one emergency away from bankruptcy.

Brad set out to change that. When he first called me about
Invest America in 2020, I thought it was a fool’s errand. Six years later, nearly 70 million children have accounts in their name, and every American newborn receives $1,000 in the S&P 500. The challenge now is getting families to claim their accounts, since free money is surprisingly hard to give away.

Brad and Geoffrey believe even a small nest egg, when given a head start on compounding, can help rebuild faith in capitalism. As AI reshapes the economy, they see these accounts as the basis of a new social contract built on ownership and participation, where every child owns a piece of the upside.

Please enjoy my conversation with Brad and Geoffrey.
